summary.title: UniVidX: A Unified Multimodal Framework for Versatile Video Generation via Diffusion Priors

setting_and_object.category: Algorithm / Framework (fine-tuning recipe for video diffusion models)

details: Video-diffusion-based multimodal graphics methods train a separate network per fixed input-output mapping (e.g. RGB->normal), losing flexibility and ignoring correlations across aligned visual modalities, which yields cross-modal inconsistency.
Goal: one model in which any subset of pixel-aligned modalities can act as condition or target, while preserving the pretrained text-to-video backbone's priors.

UniVidX: a unified fine-tuning framework on a T2V diffusion backbone where all modality latents are concatenated along the batch dimension (never channel-wise), so input/output structures are untouched.

Stochastic Condition Masking: during training modalities are randomly partitioned into clean conditions (timestep fixed at t=1) and noisy flow-matching targets, teaching omni-directional conditional generation (Text->X, X->X, Text&X->X).

Decoupled Gated LoRA: per-modality LoRA adapters gated on so they act only when that modality is a generation target (bypassed when it is a clean condition); plus Cross-Modal Self-Attention sharing keys/values across modalities with modality-specific queries.
UniVid-Intrinsic: RGB + albedo + irradiance + normal (roughness/metallic/depth deliberately excluded); tasks include text-to-intrinsic, inverse rendering, forward rendering.

UniVid-Alpha: blended RGB + alpha matte (replicated to 3 channels for the frozen VAE) + foreground + background (background is inpainted behind the subject); tasks include text-to-RGBA and auxiliary-free video matting.
Together 15 distinct tasks across three paradigms; compositions enable relighting, retexturing, material editing, inpainting, background/foreground replacement.
Wan2.1-T2V-14B frozen backbone, LoRA rank 32 per modality, 385M trainable parameters; flow-matching velocity loss on target latents only.
AdamW, cosine annealing 1e-4 -> 1e-6, BF16, 4x H100, 21-frame clips, batch size 1/GPU; 6,000 steps (Intrinsic) and 5,000 steps (Alpha).
InteriorVid: self-built Blender/Cycles synthetic dataset from 167 3D indoor scenes, 924 clips of 21 frames at 480x640 with EXR 16-bit albedo/irradiance/normal; 900 train / 24 test.
UniVid-Alpha trained on 484 human-centric videos from VideoMatte240K at 432x768; captions generated with Qwen3-VL.
Evaluation also on real/out-of-domain benchmarks: MAW (real albedo), Sintel (normals), VideoMatte.
Intrinsics/rendering: RGB<->X, Diffusion Renderer, Ouroboros; normals: Stable Normal, Lotus, NormalCrafter, DSINE, GeoWizard, GenPercept, Marigold-E2E-FT.
Generation: IntrinsiX (text-to-intrinsic, image-level) and LayerDiffuse (text-to-RGBA, image-level).
Matting: auxiliary-free RVM, MODNet, VMFormer; mask-guided AdaM, FTP-VM, MaGGIe, MatAnyone.
Channel-concatenation variant of both models instead of batch concatenation.
'w/o Dec.': single shared rank-64 LoRA (matched parameter count) plus per-modality RoPE offsets.
'w/o Gating': LoRAs always active (m_k = 1); 'w/ Van.': vanilla per-modality self-attention instead of CMSA.
Multi-condition vs single-condition perception paths (RGB vs RGB+albedo -> normal).

key_findings.finding: A single batch-concatenated, LoRA-adapted T2V model can perform omni-directional multimodal video generation and match or beat task-specific state of the art with under 1k training videos.
key_findings.evidence: On InteriorVid-Test UniVid-Intrinsic leads all baselines: albedo 16.89 PSNR vs 14.21 (Ouroboros), irradiance 13.46 vs 11.29 (RGB<->X), normal MAE 11.09 deg vs 12.49 (NormalCrafter), forward rendering 15.31 PSNR vs 13.48; on real MAW it gets the best intensity error 0.44 despite synthetic-only training; UniVid-Alpha attains best MAD 4.24 / MSE 0.69 / Grad 1.86 / dtSSD 1.39 on VideoMatte, beating even mask-guided methods while also outputting a clean background.

key_findings.finding: Batch-dimension concatenation is essential for data efficiency: the common channel-concatenation paradigm collapses under small data because it disrupts pretrained priors.
key_findings.evidence: Variants of both models trained with channel-concatenated latents (requiring retrained input conv and new output heads) produce severely corrupted albedo and foreground outputs, whereas the batch-concatenated models are high fidelity at <1k videos; prior channel-concat methods use ~350K videos.

key_findings.finding: Per-modality decoupled LoRAs are what enable robust layer/modality separation, including generation from a single shared text prompt.
key_findings.evidence: Attention-map analysis at DiT block 20 shows FG and BG branches cleanly attending to subject vs background for the full model but chaotic, leaking maps for the shared-LoRA 'w/o Dec.' variant; 'w/o Dec.' confuses foreground and background in text-to-RGBA under both distinct and shared prompts, and LayerDiffuse (also shared-parameter) fails with a shared prompt while UniVid-Alpha succeeds.

key_findings.finding: Gating LoRAs off for clean conditioning inputs materially improves quality by keeping the backbone's native encoding intact.
key_findings.evidence: Always-on LoRA ('w/o Gating') degrades albedo PSNR from 16.89 to 15.02 (-1.87 dB), irradiance 13.46 -> 12.04, and normal MAE 11.09 -> 13.01 deg with 11.25-deg accuracy dropping 70.52 -> 59.75, plus visible texture loss.

key_findings.finding: Highly data-efficient normal estimation and clear benefit from flexible multi-condition inference paths.
key_findings.evidence: On Sintel the model reaches 33.5 mean / 25.8 median angular error using only 19K training frames vs NormalCrafter's 860K (>45x less), ranking third overall; and feeding RGB+albedo instead of RGB alone recovers geometry of a blurry distant object that the RGB-only path ignores.
